ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is △WSR, and on the right side is △TRV. Points W, R, T are on the same straight line, WR is labeled x+6, and RT is labeled 2x+6; points S, R, V are on another straight line. Side WS is labeled 8, and side TV is labeled 10. In the figure, there is an identical angle mark at W and at T, indicating that these two angles are equal. Reasoning: Because line WRT and line SRV intersect at R, the R angle of △WSR and the R angle of △TRV are vertical angles and are equal; and because the marking in the figure shows that ∠W and ∠T are equal, △WSR ∼ △TRV. The corresponding sides are WR ↔ RT, WS ↔ TV, so the proportion is (x+6)/(2x+6)=8/10. Solving gives 10(x+6)=8(2x+6), namely 10x+60=16x+48, so 12=6x, x=2. Therefore RT=2x+6=2(2)+6=10.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two triangles, △WSR on the left and △TRV on the right. From the image, W, R, T are collinear with WR labeled x+6 and RT labeled 2x+6; S, R, V are collinear; WS is labeled 8 and TV is labeled 10; the angles at W and T are marked congruent. Use the vertical angles at R plus the marked angles to conclude △WSR ∼ △TRV by AA. Match corresponding sides WR ↔ RT and WS ↔ TV, so (x+6)/(2x+6)=8/10. Solve for x, then compute RT=2x+6, giving 10.
